 CONSENT ITEMS  COMMENTS/ RECOMMENDATIONS
 1.  Receive Report and Discuss the  The Council discussed the management and
  Management of the Community Forest  expansion of San Dimas' urban forest. It was
  noted by a member of the public that the
  city' s tree planting history, includes 2, 200
  trees planted from 2006 to 2014 at a rate of
  200- 225 per year. The current plan aims to
  plant 60 trees annually, with 30 being new.
  The city maintains 8, 685 trees worth $ 40. 48
  million. Challenges include resident
  objections to tree planting in front yard
  easements and infrastructure  issues.
  Proposed solutions include increasing the
  budget to $ 20, 000430, 000, using Metro
  funds, and creating an endowment for tree
  maintenance.  The council agreed to continue
  the discussion at a future study session.

  Council requested additional analysis and
  materials for the follow- up discussion:

  Provide additional analysis and
  materials for that follow- up discussion,
  including:
  Maps and data on identified
  planting opportunities ( the 43
  street segments / 32 street

  exist.
  Feasibility analysis for

  resident acceptance).
  Exploration of areas with low

  heat island" conditions,
  especially along streets like

  Historic council budget

  How Metro ( Gold Line)

  tree/ landscape

  drawing from the
  General Fund.
  Estimates of lifetime costs and
  benefits per tree ( planting,
  pruning, hardscape repair vs.
  environmental/ health benefits).

  Council also gave clear policy -leaning
  direction ( for staff to plan within), even though
  it was not adopted as a formal policy yet:
  o not resume planting trees in
  front -yard easements without resident
  consent; the Council expressed  broad
  opposition to " forcing" trees on
  unwilling  property owners.

  Be open to expanding the urban
  forest, but in a fiscally responsible
  way, prioritizing:
  Locations where lifetime costs
  are lower (e. g., minimal
  hardscape  impact).

  Areas with significant canopy
  gaps and higher heat impacts.
  Explore creative options such as:
  An endowment model to fund
  lifecycle maintenance of trees.
  An " adopt a tree" / "
  plant a
  tree" program where residents
  can voluntarily fund or co -fund
  trees in front of their homes.

The meeting was adjourned at 7: 00 PM.
